answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
answerStage.answerDesign: 정답 문장인 'This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is shown in his artwork.'에서 선행사인 'an attachment'를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사절 'that is shown in...'의 수동태 형태 'is shown'을 준동사 능동 표현인 'showing'으로 오류 변형합니다. 'that showing...'이 되면 주격 관계대명사 that 뒤에 서술어 역할을 할 정동사(finite verb)가 없어 문장이 통사적으로 불완전하며 비문이 됩니다. 이 자리에 분사 showing을 그대로 둘 경우 주어를 서술하는 정동사가 성립하지 않으므로, 어떠한 해석으로도 비문임을 피할 수 없습니다.

answer.surroundingText: This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is shown in his artwork.

answerStage.explanation: 관계대명사 that은 문장에서 주어 역할을 하며, 뒤에는 절을 이끄는 정동사가 이어져야 합니다. showing은 준동사인 분사로, 단독으로 동사 자리에 올 수 없습니다. 따라서 선행사(an attachment)가 보여지는 대상이므로 수동태를 완성하는 정동사인 'is shown'으로 고쳐야 어법상 올바른 문장이 됩니다.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is shown in his artwork.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, where he worked as a freelance artist.

markedExpressions.label: (C)

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: He drew inspiration from both past and present, but like all successful artists, his sculpture transcends race and language.

markedExpressions.label: (E)

wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 선행사 Santa Fe를 수식하며 뒤에 완전한 절(he worked as a freelance artist)이 이어지므로 관계부사 where의 사용은 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 주어 Houser's designs가 전통에 '뿌리내린' 수동적 의미이므로 (are) 다음에 이어지는 과거분사 rooted는 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 주어 his sculpture가 3인칭 단수이므로 단수 동사 transcends로 수일치한 것은 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 대명사 it이 가리키는 조각품이 감상되는 대상이므로 수동태를 구성하는 과거분사 appreciated는 어법상 올바른 표현입니다.

question.explanation: 관계대명사 that은 문장에서 주어 역할을 하며, 뒤에는 절을 이끄는 정동사가 이어져야 합니다. showing은 준동사인 분사로, 단독으로 동사 자리에 올 수 없습니다. 따라서 선행사(an attachment)가 보여지는 대상이므로 수동태를 완성하는 정동사인 'is shown'으로 고쳐야 어법상 올바른 문장이 됩니다.
keyPoints: (A) 정동사 vs 준동사 — 관계절의 정동사 필요성 판단
(B) 관계대명사 vs 관계부사 — 뒤따르는 절의 완전성 파악
(D) 주어-동사 수일치 — 주어의 인칭 및 수 파악
question.passageWithMarkers: Allan Houser created contemporary Apache sculpture. As a child, he listened to his father's stories about the adventures of Chief Geronimo. This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that __(A) showing__ in his artwork. Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, __(B) where__ he worked as a freelance artist. During World War II, he traveled to California, where he became interested in the media of sculpture. He created works in a variety of styles and mastered bronze, metal, and stone sculpture. Houser's designs are modern, yet firmly __(C) rooted__ in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers. He drew inspiration from both past and present, but like all successful artists, his sculpture __(D) transcends__ race and language. The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can be __(E) appreciated__ by anyone, regardless of his or her background.

passageText: Allan Houser created contemporary Apache sculpture. As a child, he listened to his father's stories about the adventures of Chief Geronimo. This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is shown in his artwork. Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, where he worked as a freelance artist. During World War II, he traveled to California, where he became interested in the media of sculpture. He created works in a variety of styles and mastered bronze, metal, and stone sculpture. Houser's designs are modern, yet firmly rooted in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers. He drew inspiration from both past and present, but like all successful artists, his sculpture transcends race and language. The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can be appreciated by anyone, regardless of his or her background.

answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
answerStage.answerDesign: 정답 문장은 'Consider joining a reading group...'입니다. 명령문 형태인 정동사 'Consider'를 준동사 'Considering'으로 변형하여 문장 전체에 정동사가 존재하지 않도록 비문을 만들었습니다. 'Considering'으로 교체될 경우 전체 문장 'Considering joining a reading group wherein...' 내에 주절의 본동사(정동사)가 없어지므로 통사적으로 성립할 수 없습니다. 뒤따르는 분사구문 등으로 재해석하려 해도 쉼표 뒤에 주절이 없으므로 명백한 비문입니다.

answer.surroundingText: Reading can be sociable. Consider joining a reading group in which everybody takes turns reading aloud from a novel.

answerStage.explanation: 한 문장에는 반드시 주절을 이끄는 정동사가 하나 존재해야 합니다. 'Reading can be sociable.' 뒤에 이어지는 문장에서는 주어가 생략된 명령문 형태로 정동사 Consider가 문장을 시작해야 올바른 문장이 됩니다. 이를 준동사인 Considering으로 바꾸면 문장 전체에 정동사가 없게 되어 어법상 틀린 비문이 됩니다. 따라서 정동사 형태인 Consider로 고쳐야 합니다.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 전치사 of의 목적어 자리에 동명사가 왔으며, 남겨진다는 수동의 의미이므로 수동형 동명사 being left가 올바르게 쓰였습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 선행사 other people을 수식하는 주격 관계대명사 who가 올바르게 사용되었습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 지각동사 see의 목적어 someone else가 몰입된 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 immersed가 목적격 보어로 적절히 쓰였습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 동명사구인 Reading a book collaboratively가 주어이므로 단수 동사 is로 수일치한 것은 어법상 올바릅니다.

question.explanation: 이 문장은 '[Considering joining a reading group ...] in which [everybody takes turns reading aloud from a novel]' 구조를 가지고 있습니다. 문장에 주절의 역할을 하는 정동사가 전혀 없습니다. 따라서 Considering을 명령문을 구성하는 정동사 Consider로 고쳐야 합니다.
keyPoints: (D) 정동사 vs 준동사 — 주절을 완결할 정동사의 필요성 판단
(B) 관계대명사의 격과 선행사 수일치
(E) 주어-동사 수일치 — 동명사구 주어는 단수 취급
question.passageWithMarkers: We all enjoy the pleasure of __(A) being left__ alone with a good book. But sometimes after several hours of immersion we lift our heads and look around, suddenly struck by the quiet, the absence of others. In this situation, we are suffering from reading-induced loneliness. The solution is to read in the company of other people __(B) who__ are reading - whether in a public space such as a café or a library, or in your own home, with your reading friend or partner at the other end of the sofa. Next time you look up, you'll see someone else similarly __(C) immersed__, and you won't feel alone at all. Reading can be sociable. __(D) Considering__ joining a reading group in which everybody takes turns reading aloud from a novel. Reading a book collaboratively __(E) is__ a wonderful way to share an otherwise internal and solitary experience.

passageText: We all enjoy the pleasure of being left alone with a good book. But sometimes after several hours of immersion we lift our heads and look around, suddenly struck by the quiet, the absence of others. In this situation, we are suffering from reading-induced loneliness. The solution is to read in the company of other people who are reading - whether in a public space such as a café or a library, or in your own home, with your reading friend or partner at the other end of the sofa. Next time you look up, you'll see someone else similarly immersed, and you won't feel alone at all. Reading can be sociable. Consider joining a reading group in which everybody takes turns reading aloud from a novel. Reading a book collaboratively is a wonderful way to share an otherwise internal and solitary experience.

answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
answerStage.answerDesign: 정답 문장인 'If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX qualifies as a technology...'에서 주어인 'a thousand lines'는 'lines'가 핵(head)인 복수 명사구이므로 단수 동사인 qualifies는 어법상 비문입니다. 복합 명사구 내부의 전치사구 수식을 받는 주어 명사구의 핵심 명사는 'lines'이므로 수일치 법칙에 따라 복수 동사인 qualify가 오는 것이 옳습니다. 이를 단수형인 'qualifies'로 바꿈으로써, 주어 자리에 있는 'a thousand lines'가 복수형임에도 'a thousand' 또는 단수 개념으로 혼동하여 수일치 오류를 범하게 유도하였습니다. 다른 해석으로 보아도 'lines'가 주어의 핵심임은 불변하므로 명백한 비문입니다.

answer.surroundingText: If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX qualify as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet) must qualify as well.

answerStage.explanation: If절의 주어 부 핵심 명사는 복수형인 'lines'(a thousand lines of letters in UNIX)이므로, 이에 호응하는 동사는 복수형인 qualify가 되어야 합니다. 단수 동사인 qualifies는 복수 주어와 수일치가 맞지 않아 어법상 틀린 표현입니다.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We tend to think of technology as shiny tools and gadgets.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Even if we acknowledge that technology can exist in disembodied form,

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX qualifies as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet) must qualify as well.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: They are something useful produced by a mind.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies responsible for a Lord of the Rings movie.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 명사 tools and gadgets를 수식하는 형용사로서 shiny가 올바르게 사용되었습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 부사절 주어 we의 정동사로서 현재형 acknowledge가 올바르게 사용되었습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 단일 개념으로 취급된 주어 a thousand lines of letters in UNIX에 호응하는 단수 동사 qualifies가 올바르게 사용되었습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 명사 technologies를 뒤에서 수식하는 형용사구의 핵으로 형용사 responsible이 적절합니다.

question.explanation: 선행하는 대명사 something을 수식하는 분사의 능동/수동 관계를 묻고 있습니다. 수식을 받는 something이 mind(마음)에 의해 '생산되는' 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 지닙니다. 의미상 수동 관계를 나타내므로 현재분사 producing은 비문입니다. 따라서 producing을 과거분사 produced로 고쳐야 합니다.
keyPoints: (D) 분사능수동 — 명사를 수식하는 분사의 능동/수동 관계 판단.
(C) 수일치 — 주어의 단수/복수 개념 취급에 따른 수일치 판단.
(E) 형부자리 — 명사 뒤에서 후치 수식하는 형용사 자리 판단.
question.passageWithMarkers: We tend to think of technology as __(A) shiny__ tools and gadgets. Even if we __(B) acknowledge__ that technology can exist in disembodied form, such as software, we tend not to include in this category paintings, literature, music, dance, poetry, and the arts in general. But we should. If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX __(C) qualifies__ as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet) must qualify as well. They both can change our behavior, alter the course of events, or enable future inventions. A Shakespeare sonnet and a Schubert symphony, then, are in the same category as Google's search engine and the smartphone: They are something useful __(D) producing__ by a mind. We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies __(E) responsible__ for a Lord of the Rings movie. The literary rendering of the original novel is as much an invention as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures. Both are useful works of the human imagination. Both influence audiences powerfully. Both are technological.

passageText: We tend to think of technology as shiny tools and gadgets. Even if we acknowledge that technology can exist in disembodied form, such as software, we tend not to include in this category paintings, literature, music, dance, poetry, and the arts in general. But we should. If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX qualifies as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet) must qualify as well. They both can change our behavior, alter the course of events, or enable future inventions. A Shakespeare sonnet and a Schubert symphony, then, are in the same category as Google's search engine and the smartphone: They are something useful produced by a mind. We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies responsible for a Lord of the Rings movie. The literary rendering of the original novel is as much an invention as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures. Both are useful works of the human imagination. Both influence audiences powerfully. Both are technological.

answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
answerStage.answerDesign: 정답 문장인 'This so-called "negativity bias" can keep you focused on what's going wrong'에서 'keep'의 목적격 보어로 사용된 과거분사 'focused'를 현재분사 'focusing'으로 변경합니다. 목적어인 'you'가 부정적 편향에 의해 (강제로) '초점이 맞춰진' 수동적 대상이 되므로 과거분사 focused가 적절합니다. 만약 focusing으로 쓰인다면 주위나 대상 따위에 목적어 스스로 능동적으로 초점을 맞추는 진행 중인 동작이 되어, 문맥상 '부정적 왜곡에 의해 사로잡혀 초점이 맞춰진 것'이라는 수동적 의미에 어조가 어긋나며 어법상 목적어를 도취시키지 않고 'focusing on'의 제약과 결합할 때 부적절한 비문이 됩니다. 따라서 focused가 맞고, focusing은 오답입니다.

answer.surroundingText: This so-called "negativity bias" can keep you focused on what's going wrong (which explains why complaining is such a popular pastime).

answerStage.explanation: keep의 목적어인 you가 (부정적 편향에 의해) 무언가에 정신이 팔려 '초점이 맞춰지게 되는' 대상이므로, 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 focused가 오는 것이 어법상 올바릅니다. 목적어와 목적격 보어의 관계가 능동이 아닌 수동이므로 능동 의미의 현재분사 focusing은 비문이 됩니다.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

question.explanation: 주격 관계대명사 that이 이끄는 관계절의 선행사는 앞선 명사구 a recent win을 부연 설명하는 단수 대명사인 anything입니다. 선행사가 3인칭 단수이므로 주격 관계대명사 뒤에 이어지는 동사 역시 단수형으로 수일치해야 하므로, 복수형 동사인 give를 쓰면 이 자리에서 명백한 비문이 됩니다. 따라서 수일치 규칙을 따르기 위해 give를 gives로 고쳐야 합니다. 학생들이 괄호 안의 삽입구에서 수식을 받는 대명사의 수를 단수로 정확하게 파악할 수 있어야 문맥을 올바로 이해할 수 있습니다.
keyPoints: (E) 단수/복수 수일치 — 주격 관계대명사 절의 동사와 선행사 수일치
(A) 목적격 보어 — 목적어를 서술하는 형용사 보어 판별
(C) 정동사 자리 — 명령문 주절의 술어 동사 확인
question.passageWithMarkers: The human brain is wired to look for threats - a trait that kept us __(A) alive__ when we were living on the savannas but that can prevent happiness in our modern lives. This so-called "negativity bias" can keep you focused on what's going wrong (which explains __(B) why__ complaining is such a popular pastime). To break out of this neural rut, __(C) train__ yourself to acknowledge when things go right. If you keep a calendar or a journal, make a point __(D) to write__ down what went well. If you're more of a verbal processor, start your conversations with friends by sharing a recent win (anything that __(E) give__ you that yesssss feeling). Where the mind goes, reality follows. The more you appreciate life, the more reasons you have to celebrate it.

passageText: The human brain is wired to look for threats - a trait that kept us alive when we were living on the savannas but that can prevent happiness in our modern lives. This so-called "negativity bias" can keep you focused on what's going wrong (which explains why complaining is such a popular pastime). To break out of this neural rut, train yourself to acknowledge when things go right. If you keep a calendar or a journal, make a point to write down what went well. If you're more of a verbal processor, start your conversations with friends by sharing a recent win (anything that gives you that yesssss feeling). Where the mind goes, reality follows. The more you appreciate life, the more reasons you have to celebrate it.

question.passageWithMarkers: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode __(A) what__ we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than __(B) retrieving__ the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail __(C) struggling__ to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as __(D) abstract__ ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than __(E) played__ back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.

passageText: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.

passageText: For many of us, making time for exercise is a continuing challenge. Between work commitments and family obligations, it often feels like there's no room in our packed schedules for a dedicated workout. But what if the workout came to you, right in the midst of your daily routine? That's where the beauty of integrating mini-exercises into household chores comes into play. question.passageWithMarkers: We have all had the experience of suddenly __(A) noticing__ that a source of constant background noise, such as a distant jackhammer or music from a store, has just ceased - yet we hadn't noticed the sound while it was ongoing. Your auditory areas were predicting its continuation, moment after moment, and as long as the noise didn't change you __(B) paying__ it no attention. By ceasing, it violated your prediction and __(C) attracted__ your attention. Here's a historical example. Right after New York City stopped running elevated trains, people called the police in the middle of the night __(D) claiming__ that something woke them up. passageText: We have all had the experience of suddenly noticing that a source of constant background noise, such as a distant jackhammer or music from a store, has just ceased - yet we hadn't noticed the sound while it was ongoing. Your auditory areas were predicting its continuation, moment after moment, and as long as the noise didn't change you paid it no attention. By ceasing, it violated your prediction and attracted your attention. Here's a historical example. Right after New York City stopped running elevated trains, people called the police in the middle of the night claiming that something woke them up. They tended to call around the time the trains used to run past their apartments.

passageText: The fast pace of today's lifestyle has us piling one thing on top of another. But you should know that multitasking doesn't save any time. Very often, multitasking only slows you down, contrary to popular belief. Give your whole focus to what you're doing at the moment no matter what it is. While doing the laundry, just do the laundry: Listen to the sound of the water as it fills the washing machine and feel the clothes in your hand. It doesn't take up any more time than it would when done with your phone pressed to your ear. The same applies to your work. Focus on one task at a time, and you'll accomplish each task better, and probably faster.

answerStage.answerDesign: 정답 문장 인용: 'The moment that occurs, the rest of the penguins watch with anticipation to see what happens next.'/ 오류 변형: occurs → occurring/ 이 자리에서 비문인 통사적 이유: 'The moment [that occurs]'에서 'The moment'는 '~하는 순간에'라는 부사절 접속사 역할을 하며, 이끄는 부사절 속에 주어(that)와 서술어 동사(occurs)가 완전하게 갖춰져야 합니다. 현재분사인 occurring으로 바꾸면 부사절 내의 정동사가 사라져 비문이 됩니다. / 반증 검사: occurring을 분사구문이나 후치수식어로 해석하더라도, 부사절을 이끌 접속사 역할을 수행하는 'The moment' 뒤에서 주어 역할을 하는 관계 사절이나 지시대명사 'that'을 술어동사 없이 수식하는 구조가 되어 여전히 비문입니다.

answer.surroundingText: The moment that occurs, the rest of the penguins watch with anticipation to see what happens next. If the pioneer survives, everyone else will follow suit.

answerStage.explanation: the moment는 '~하는 순간에'라는 뜻으로 부사절 접속사 역할을 합니다. 따라서 그 뒤에는 '주어 + 동사'의 완전한 절의 형태가 이어져야 합니다. 지시 대명사인 주어 that을 받아 절을 완결할 정동사가 필요하므로, 준동사 형태인 occurring은 어법상 적절하지 않으며 정동사인 occurs로 고쳐야 합니다.

passageText: There is a critical factor that determines whether your choice will influence that of others: the visible consequences of the choice. Take the case of the Adélie penguins. They are often found strolling in large groups toward the edge of the water in search of food. Yet danger awaits in the icy-cold water. There is the leopard seal, for one, which likes to have penguins for a meal. What is an Adélie to do? The penguins' solution is to play the waiting game. They wait and wait and wait by the edge of the water until one of them gives up and jumps in. The moment that occurs, the rest of the penguins watch with anticipation to see what happens next. If the pioneer survives, everyone else will follow suit. If it perishes, they'll turn away. One penguin's destiny alters the fate of all the others. Their strategy, you could say, is "learn and live."

'going'이 올 경우 이 절은 동사가 결여된 비문이 되며, 이를 준동사적 용법의 다른 구문으로 해석할 여지(예: 분사구문 등)도 존재하지 않는 명백한 비문입니다.

question.passageWithMarkers: We tend to go long periods of time without __(A) reaching__ out to the people we know. Then, we suddenly take notice of the distance __(B) that__ has formed and we scramble to make repairs. We call people we haven't spoken to in ages, __(C) hoping__ that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance we've created. However, this rarely works: relationships aren't kept up with big one-time fixes. They're kept up with regular maintenance, like a car. In our relationships, we have to make sure that not too much time __(D) going__ by between oil changes, so to speak. This isn't to say that you shouldn't bother __(E) calling__ someone just because it's been a while since you've spoken; just that it's more ideal not to let yourself fall out of touch in the first place. Consistency always brings better results.

passageText: We tend to go long periods of time without reaching out to the people we know. Then, we suddenly take notice of the distance that has formed and we scramble to make repairs. We call people we haven't spoken to in ages, hoping that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance we've created. However, this rarely works: relationships aren't kept up with big one-time fixes. They're kept up with regular maintenance, like a car. In our relationships, we have to make sure that not too much time goes by between oil changes, so to speak. This isn't to say that you shouldn't bother calling someone just because it's been a while since you've spoken; just that it's more ideal not to let yourself fall out of touch in the first place. Consistency always brings better results.
